newsitem.title: UK: BoE's George - UK still lacks inflation credibility.
newsitem.headline: BoE's George - UK still lacks inflation credibility.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Monday that the credibility of Britain's monetary authorities was still being damaged by the view that inflation was more comfortably tolerated here than in other countries.
"We are still perceived as being rather more tolerant of inflation than others, and so we don't have as much credibility as most of the others do," George told a House of Commons select committee.
"Our inflation performance compared with the rest of the world has been bad. It is still not good," he said, while adding that the performance had improved significantly.
George said that part of the problem was that Britain's inflation performance was still being viewed from a historical stance.
"Our performnace internationally is not as good as we like to think it is domestically," he said.
He said a key factor in bringing inflation down was convincing the public and financial markets that the authorities will deliver.
"We need to get people to behave in a way (which shows) they really think we will deliver inflation of 2.5 percent or less," George said.
The government's rolling target is for underlying inflation of 2.5 percent.
